9	We employ Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA)~\cite{kornblith2019} alongside RSA as a complementary perspective.
10	While RSA captures local geometric alignment via rank-order preservation, CKA measures global representational similarity through kernel-based comparisons.
11	
12	We compute both \emph{linear CKA}, which uses a linear kernel and is sensitive to second-order statistics, and \emph{RDM kernel CKA}, which operates on the same distance matrices as RSA but aggregates them differently.
13	Using both variants tests whether conclusions about representation structure are robust to the choice of similarity metric.
14	
15	Linear CKA between high-dimensional representations (4{,}096-D for LLM layers) and the 7-D action space is subject to a known dimension mismatch: the linear kernel in the low-dimensional space may not capture the same structure as in the high-dimensional space.
16	RDM kernel CKA avoids this issue by operating on distance matrices of equal size regardless of the original feature dimensionality.

\paragraph{Training redistributes geometry, enhances decodability.}
Training shifts the image\_mean RSA peak from L0 to L12 with a modest best-vs-best gain ($\Delta = +0.017$, $3\%$; Table~\ref{tab:training_effects}; Figure~\ref{fig:factorial}).
LIBERO-Spatial confirms with $\Delta = +0.023$, $4\%$, $p < 0.001$ (\S\ref{sec:cross_benchmark}), suggesting the LIBERO-Goal CI (incl.\ zero) reflects limited power.
$R^2$ best-vs-best shows larger improvements: image\_mean $\Delta = +0.015$ ($p = 0.006$), readout $\Delta = +0.069$ ($p < 0.0001$).
At L12, training produces a large same-layer effect ($\Delta = +0.079$, $p < 0.0001$), confirming that training has a dramatic effect on \emph{where} geometry peaks but only a modest effect on \emph{how high}.
Untrained image\_mean $R^2$ drops below zero at L10--L11 ($R^2 = -0.33$, $-0.28$); training converts this pathological zone into the network's peak.

\paragraph{Cross-benchmark validation (LIBERO-Spatial).}
\label{sec:cross_benchmark}
The inverted-U replicates on LIBERO-Spatial (10 out-of-distribution tasks; Appendix~\ref{sec:cross_benchmark_appendix}): trained image\_mean RSA peaks at L14 ($\rho = 0.691$), $R^2$ at L13 ($0.696$), with peaks shifting ${\sim}2$ layers deeper---consistent with increased task difficulty.
RSA--$R^2$ peak convergence does not replicate (6-layer gap vs.\ $|\Delta_\text{layer}| = 1$ on Goal), suggesting this alignment may be benchmark-specific.
These findings are robust to distance metric choice, hold across all action dimensions, survive permutation testing, and replicate under halved demonstration counts (RSA profile $r = 0.970$; Appendix~\ref{sec:robustness_appendix}).
